title: LSST Strong Lensing Systems Dark Matter Sensitivity Analysis with Neural Ratio Estimators
summary: Strong gravitational lensing offers a unique probe of dark matter (DM) on sub-galactic scales, where the abundance and distribution of low-mass halos are highly sensitive to the underlying properties of DM particles. In this work, we forecast LSST's sensitivity to DM substructure in galaxy-galaxy strong lenses using simulated samples and neural ratio estimators (NREs). Our simulations include both subhalos within the main deflector and line-of-sight (LOS) halos, with halo masses down to $\sim 10^7 M_\odot$ under the expected LSST ten-year survey imaging quality. We show that the constraining power on halo mass function (HMF) parameters improves significantly with sample size. Analyses based on a few hundred lenses yield broad posteriors comparable with other probes like the Ly-$α$ forest. By contrast, when combining 2500 lenses, $\approx 74\%$ and $\approx 36\%$ of the prior volume considered can be excluded at the $3σ$ and $5σ$ levels respectively, enabling statistically significant exclusions of non-$Λ$CDM scenarios. We further demonstrate that the sensitivity arises not only from the high-mass end of the HMF but also from low-mass halos: masking halos below $\log (m_{\rm halo}/M_\odot) \leq 7.5$ induces a measurable shift in the inferred posteriors. Finally, we find that LOS halos contribute significantly to the constraining power, with increasing importance of LOS halos at higher redshifts. While this analysis assumes perfect knowledge of the data-generating process and cannot be directly applied to data analysis, it quantifies constraints achievable with LSST alone and motivates the development of robust inference methods for real survey data.

AI.tldr: This study forecasts LSST's ability to constrain dark matter halo properties via strong gravitational lensing and neural ratio estimators, showing that large samples can exclude alternative DM models with high confidence, emphasizing the importance of low-mass and line-of-sight halos in achieving these constraints.
AI.motivation: To probe dark matter properties on sub-galactic scales by analyzing low-mass halo abundance and distribution using strong gravitational lensing, leveraging upcoming LSST data.
AI.method: Simulations of galaxy-galaxy strong lensing including subhalos and line-of-sight halos down to $\sim 10^7 M_\odot$ combined with neural ratio estimators for statistical inference on halo mass function parameters.
AI.result: Demonstrated that larger samples of lenses (up to 2500) significantly tighten constraints on dark matter halo mass function parameters, excluding non-$\Lambda$CDM models at high significance, with sensitivity arising from both low and high-mass halos; line-of-sight halos notably improve constraints, especially at higher redshifts.
AI.conclusion: LSST's ten-year survey has the potential to provide strong statistical constraints on dark matter substructure through strong lensing, motivating further development of robust inference methods applicable to real data.

title: A Natural $\gtrsim 100\times$ Telescope: Discovery of the Strongly Lensed Type II SN 2025mkn at $z=1.37$
comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, submitted to ApJL
summary: We present the discovery of SN 2025mkn, a gravitationally lensed Type II supernova. First detected as a blue transient in ZTF, 0.83$^{\prime\prime}$ from a $z=0.42$ elliptical galaxy, follow-up SNIFS/UH2.2m and LRIS/Keck spectra revealed absorption lines at $z=1.371$. Later JWST NIRCam imaging shows that the bright transient is a close pair of point sources separated by $\sim 0.07^{\prime\prime}$, and a 30 times fainter counterimage opposite the lens, for which NIRSpec reveals strong H$α$ emission also at $z=1.371$. The light curves and spectra are consistent with the Type II supernova source being magnified $\gtrsim 100$ times, with $\sim 250$ required to reconcile its luminosity with that of nearby events such as SN 2023ixf. Lens models are consistent with such high magnifications, and always show that the faint image arrived first (undetected in earlier ZTF imaging), consistent with the later spectral phase of this fainter image. A fourth image is also predicted and possibly detected in the NIRSpec data. Light-curve-based time-delay measurements are not possible due to the first image being the faintest; however, the resolved NIRSpec spectra offer a future opportunity for time-delay cosmography through supernova phase measurements.

AI.tldr: SN 2025mkn is a Type II supernova at z=1.371, gravitationally lensed with over 100 times magnification by a z=0.42 galaxy, producing multiple images detected by ZTF and JWST. This event provides a unique opportunity for cosmology through time-delay studies using spectral phases.
AI.motivation: To discover and study a gravitationally lensed Type II supernova to utilize its high magnification for astrophysical insights and cosmological measurements.
AI.method: Detection via ZTF as a blue transient, followed by spectroscopic confirmation using SNIFS/UH2.2m and LRIS/Keck, imaging and spectroscopy with JWST NIRCam and NIRSpec for lensing analysis and spectral characterization, combined with lens modeling to understand magnification and image configuration.
AI.result: Identification of SN 2025mkn as a highly magnified (over 100x) Type II supernova at redshift 1.371, lensed by a foreground elliptical galaxy at z=0.42, with multiple resolved images consistent with lens models, and potential for future time-delay cosmography via spectral phase measurements.
AI.conclusion: SN 2025mkn represents a rare and extreme gravitational lensing case of a Type II supernova, enabling unprecedented magnification that facilitates detailed study and holds promise for cosmological applications through time-delay measurement using spectral data.

title: The peculiar velocity correlation function of the Cosmicflows-4 catalog
summary: We present an analysis of the parallel peculiar velocity correlation function using data from the Cosmicflows-4 (CF4) survey. CF4 significantly extends the depth of the peculiar velocity measurements, mitigating the impact of observers on the cosmic variance. We examine the distribution of cosmic variance using different velocity correlation estimators. The combination of the large peculiar velocity uncertainties and the anisotropy distribution of the CF4 data across the northern and southern hemispheres results in substantial statistical uncertainties in the velocity correlation function. To address this, we test different weighing schemes in the velocity correlation function and implement a more accurate peculiar velocity estimator that reduces velocity uncertainties, consequently decreasing the statistical uncertainty. Using the CF4 group dataset, we derive a growth rate of $fσ_8=0.384^{+0.116}_{-0.194}$ and a local growth rate of $fσ_8=0.569^{+0.054}_{-0.06}$ through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo method.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes peculiar velocity correlations in the Cosmicflows-4 survey, reduces uncertainties through improved estimators and weighting, and derives updated cosmological growth rates using MCMC methods.
AI.motivation: To analyze the parallel peculiar velocity correlation function and improve the accuracy of cosmological parameter estimation by mitigating cosmic variance and velocity uncertainties in the Cosmicflows-4 (CF4) survey data.
AI.method: Analyzed the cosmic velocity correlation using CF4 data, tested different weighting schemes, implemented a more accurate peculiar velocity estimator to reduce uncertainties, and employed Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods for parameter estimation.
AI.result: Derived a growth rate of fσ8=0.384^{+0.116}_{-0.194} and a local growth rate of fσ8=0.569^{+0.054}_{-0.06}, showing improved statistical uncertainty management and parameter constraints.
AI.conclusion: Using enhanced estimators and weighting schemes on the CF4 group dataset, the study successfully reduced statistical uncertainties in velocity correlations, enabling more accurate measurements of cosmic growth rates.

title: A Dynamical Equilibrium Linking Nanohertz Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background to Cosmic Structure Formation
summary: The stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) is conventionally treated as a passive relic of its astrophysical and cosmological sources, with negligible back-reaction on the matter content of the Universe. Here we show that this assumption needs to be modified once the SGWB and matter are treated as a dynamically coupled non-equilibrium system. Combining linearized general relativity with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, we derive a generalized Langevin framework that drives the coupled system toward a dynamical equilibrium, which is characterized by a distinctive strain spectrum with a high-frequency cutoff $\mathcal{W}$, and a scale-dependent coupling parameter that screens gravity progressively for the most massive structures. Three findings support this framework. Fitting the equilibrium spectrum to the NANOGrav 15-year dataset yields a Bayes factor of $48\pm 3.8$ over the supermassive black hole binary baseline, achieved entirely within general relativity and the Standard Model. The PTA-calibrated screening mass scale $m_{c}\sim 10^{12}\text{--}10^{14}\,M_{\odot}$ overlaps, with no free cosmological parameter, the $Λ$CDM-derived linear-to-nonlinear transition mass $M_{\rm NL}$ of cosmic structure at $\sim 8\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$. Most strikingly, promoting this concordance to a structural identification expresses $\mathcal{W}$ entirely in terms of $M_{\rm NL}$, and its inverse acquires a transparent physical reading as a coherence threshold for SGWB-matter coupling. $\mathcal{W}$ is thereby a derived quantity linking nanohertz gravitational-wave observables to the late-time cosmological sector. The framework makes distinctive scale-dependent predictions testable by forthcoming large-scale structure surveys and space-borne gravitational-wave observatories.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new dynamic coupling framework for the stochastic gravitational wave background and matter, successfully explaining NANOGrav data and connecting gravitational-wave features to cosmic structure without new physics beyond general relativity and the Standard Model.
AI.motivation: The conventional treatment of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) as a passive relic neglects potential dynamic coupling and back-reaction with the matter content of the Universe. This paper aims to revise this assumption by modeling SGWB and matter as a coupled non-equilibrium system.
AI.method: By combining linearized general relativity with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, the authors derive a generalized Langevin framework to describe the dynamical coupling between SGWB and matter. This framework predicts a dynamical equilibrium characterized by a distinctive strain spectrum with a high-frequency cutoff and a scale-dependent coupling parameter that screens gravity for massive cosmic structures.
AI.result: Fitting the proposed equilibrium spectrum to the NANOGrav 15-year dataset yields a strong Bayes factor favoring this model over traditional astrophysical sources, entirely within standard physics. The inferred screening mass scale coincides with the known linear-to-nonlinear transition mass scale of cosmic structures. This identification enables expressing the high-frequency cutoff parameter as a derived cosmological quantity, linking gravitational-wave observations to late-time cosmology. The model also produces scale-dependent predictions testable by upcoming large-scale structure and gravitational-wave observations.
AI.conclusion: Treating SGWB and matter as a dynamically coupled non-equilibrium system provides a new framework that explains recent gravitational-wave data and connects nanohertz gravitational-wave signals to cosmic structure formation. This approach suggests an intrinsic link between SGWB characteristics and cosmological mass scales, inviting further observational tests.

title: GW190711_030756 and GW200114_020818: astrophysical interpretation of two asymmetric binary black hole mergers in the IAS catalog
summary: We provide a comprehensive analysis of GW190711_030756 and GW200114_020818, two of the most significant binary black hole merger candidates in the IAS catalog, with probabilities of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro}=0.99$ and $0.71$, respectively, and signal-to-noise ratios of approximately $10.0$ and $13.4$. We employ numerical relativity surrogate models to infer both the source properties and the remnant properties of these two candidates. We find that both GW190711_030756 and GW200114_020818 are asymmetric-mass binaries, with inferred mass ratios of $0.35^{+0.32}_{-0.15}$ and $\leq 0.20$. In addition, GW200114_020818 is inferred to have a source-frame total mass of approximately $220M_{\odot}$ and highly spinning black holes, with primary (secondary) dimensionless spin magnitudes of $0.96^{+0.03}_{-0.07}$ ($0.84^{+0.13}_{-0.34}$), closely resembling GW231123_135430. We further find that GW200114\_020818 has a confidently negative effective inspiral spin of $χ_{\rm eff}=-0.60^{+0.22}_{-0.13}$ and exhibits strong spin precession, characterized by an effective precession parameter of $χ_{\rm p}=0.60^{+0.21}_{-0.19}$. GW200114_020818 (when considered alongside GW231123_135430) points towards an emerging population of massive, rapidly spinning BBH mergers. While GW231123_135430 is consistent with mergers in globular clusters, producing systems like GW200114_020818 in such environments remains difficult even under hierarchical merger scenarios. The probability that the remnant black hole of GW190711_030756 (GW200114_020818) is retained in its host environment is $0.079$ ($0.0002$), $0.62$ ($0.965$), and $0.997$ ($1$) if the merger occurred in a globular cluster, a nuclear star cluster, or an elliptical galaxy, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes two key binary black hole merger candidates, revealing asymmetric mass ratios, high spins, and strong spin precession, especially in GW200114_020818. It suggests a new population of massive, fast-spinning mergers and shows environment impacts remnant black hole retention, with elliptical galaxies being the most favorable.
AI.motivation: To analyze significant binary black hole merger candidates in the IAS catalog to understand their source and remnant properties, and to investigate the environments in which these mergers occur.
AI.method: Utilization of numerical relativity surrogate models for parameter inference of source properties (mass ratios, spins, total mass) and remnant black hole retention probabilities across different astrophysical environments.
AI.result: Both events are asymmetric-mass binaries with one showing extremely high total mass and spin magnitudes, exhibiting strong spin precession. GW200114_020818 and another event GW231123_135430 indicate a population of massive, rapidly spinning BBH mergers. Retention probabilities vary significantly across environments, with elliptical galaxies most likely to retain remnants.
AI.conclusion: The study identifies a new population of massive, highly spinning binary black hole mergers and highlights environmental influence on remnant retention, challenging globular cluster formation scenarios for certain systems.

title: Ray-traced weak lensing convergence in screened modified gravity theories
summary: Weak gravitational lensing is one of the primary cosmological probes, providing powerful constraints on the cosmological model. As Stage IV surveys are expected to deliver data of unprecedented precision, accurate modeling of weak gravitational lensing observables across both linear and non-linear scales becomes increasingly important. In this work, we investigate weak lensing in modified gravity (MG) models, extensions of the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology in which gravity deviates from general relativity, generally introducing modifications to the lensing equation. We parametrize these modifications through the common phenomenological function $Σ_\mathrm{mg}$ and apply ray-tracing to the density maps of N-body and hydrodynamical simulations. We model the time dependence of $Σ_\mathrm{mg}$ analytically, while we introduce a phenomenological scale dependence to represent the screening mechanisms by which MG models reduce to general relativity in high-density environments. Starting from the output of the FLAMINGO hydrodynamical simulations, we generate fully ray-traced convergence maps using our modified lensing model. We analyze how the parameters of our prescription affect the weak lensing convergence power spectrum and compare these effects to other known sources of variation, in particular cosmological parameters and baryonic feedback. We find that the modifications to the lensing equation deriving from the MG model produce non-negligible signatures in the convergence power spectrum and that, within extensions of the $Λ$CDM framework, these effects can be larger than those induced by baryonic physics. Our results indicate that modified lensing should become a standard ingredient of the analysis of modified gravity simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper models and analyzes weak gravitational lensing in modified gravity scenarios using simulations, finding that MG-induced modifications substantially affect the lensing power spectrum and should be standardly included in MG analyses.
AI.motivation: To accurately model weak gravitational lensing in modified gravity models, especially for high-precision Stage IV surveys.
AI.method: Parametrized modifications to the lensing equation via a phenomenological function Σ_mg with analytic time dependence and scale-dependent screening; applied ray-tracing to density maps from N-body and hydrodynamical FLAMINGO simulations to generate convergence maps.
AI.result: Modifications from MG models produce significant signatures in the weak lensing convergence power spectrum, sometimes exceeding baryonic feedback effects; indicating that such modifications should be incorporated into analyses of MG simulations.
AI.conclusion: Accurate modeling of weak gravitational lensing in modified gravity scenarios requires including modified lensing effects, as they significantly impact the convergence power spectrum beyond baryonic influences and standard cosmological parameters.

title: Detection and Evolution of Linear Polarization of the Galactic Center Transient MAXI J1744-294
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables, accepted to ApJ
summary: MAXI J1744$-$294, likely a low-mass X-ray binary system, is a Galactic-center transient source, detected at radio and X-ray wavelengths, located approximately $19''$ southeast of Sgr A*. We report the first detection of its variable linear polarization in four epochs spanning 2025 Apr 04--09. The normalized 33 and 43 GHz Stokes parameters $q$ and $u$ over the four epochs imply a common Faraday rotation screen with a rotation measure RM $=-63\,606^{+844}_{-861}$ radians m$^{-2}$, the third largest RM detected within the Galaxy. The RM is consistent with that of the Galactic center magnetar PSR J1745$-$2900, giving the first direct evidence that MAXI J1744 lies within the Galactic center region, is bound to Sgr A*, and therefore, is part of the nuclear star cluster. The uniformity in the Galactic center Faraday screen suggests that Sgr A*'s $\approx-10^5$ rad m$^{-2}$ RM is intrinsic rather than originating from an unrelated line-of-sight source. On 2025 Apr 06, we detected a secondary polarized component with an additional RM $\approx-6000$ rad m$^{-2}$, which was not seen at any other epoch. Assuming this secondary component primarily cools by synchrotron radiation, the implied local magnetic field strength is $\sim$15--30 gauss. In the context of a jetted X-ray binary progenitor, the additional RM screen and magnetic field strength are explainable with a short-lived knot in a putative jet.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first detection of variable linear polarization from MAXI J1744$-$294, confirming its location in the Galactic center via an extreme Faraday rotation measure matching that of a known magnetar. The discovery of a transient secondary RM component points to jet activity with strong magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: To investigate the localization and magnetic environment of MAXI J1744$-$294, a Galactic-center transient likely a low-mass X-ray binary, by studying its polarized radio emissions and Faraday rotation measures.
AI.method: Multi-epoch observations of 33 and 43 GHz radio linear polarization were conducted to measure normalized Stokes parameters q and u, enabling determination of the Faraday rotation measure (RM) and characterization of magnetic field properties and variability over several days.
AI.result: Detected a highly significant and variable linear polarization with a stable Faraday rotation measure RM $=-63,606^{+844}_{-861}$ rad m$^{-2}$, consistent with the Galactic center magnetar, confirming MAXI J1744's Galactic center association and binding to Sgr A*. A transient secondary polarization component with RM $	hicksim -6000$ rad m$^{-2}$ was found on one epoch, implying strong local magnetic fields (~15-30 G) likely due to a short-lived jet knot.
AI.conclusion: The consistent extreme RM confirms MAXI J1744's location and gravitational binding within the Galactic center nuclear star cluster. The intrinsic nature of Sgr A*'s large RM is supported. The transient secondary RM feature supports a dynamic jet environment in the X-ray binary progenitor.

title: Coupled Dark Energy and Dark Matter for DESI: An Effective Guide to the Phantom Divide
summary: Motivated by the recent Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 preference for dynamical dark energy, we study interacting dark energy models in which a canonical quintessence field couples to cold dark matter through a field-dependent mass $m(φ)$. In such scenarios, the effective equation of state inferred under the assumption of non-interacting dark sectors, $w_{\rm eff}(z)$, can differ from the intrinsic scalar-field equation of state $w_φ(z)$, making an apparent phantom crossing $w_{\rm eff}<-1$ possible without introducing a phantom scalar. We show that a viable realization of this mechanism requires the scalar field to originate from a frozen phase deep in the radiation era, in order for the effective coupling to remain sufficiently suppressed before recombination to evade cosmic microwave background constraints, and for the late-time evolution to become strong enough to reproduce the apparent behavior of $w_{\rm eff}(z)$ preferred by DESI. We identify the general conditions that allow these requirements to be satisfied simultaneously, and present an illustrative phenomenological realization in which $w_{\rm eff}(z)$ evolves from $w_{\rm eff}\approx -1.2$ at $z \approx 1.0$ to $w_{\rm eff}\approx -0.9$ at $z\approx 0.4$. These conditions and requirements serve as a guide for designing future models of this kind which can safely navigate the phantom divide at $w=-1$ in an effective way without phantom fields.

AI.tldr: The paper studies interacting dark energy models where a quintessence field couples to dark matter, enabling the effective equation of state to cross the phantom divide without phantom fields. By starting the scalar field frozen in the radiation era and allowing late-time strong coupling, the model reproduces DESI observations, providing guidelines for future theoretical designs.
AI.motivation: Address the DESI DR2 data suggesting preference for dynamical dark energy by investigating interacting dark energy models with a quintessence field and cold dark matter coupling.
AI.method: Model interacting dark energy by coupling a canonical quintessence field to cold dark matter via a field-dependent mass m(φ), analyze the effective equation of state w_eff(z) under non-interacting assumptions and establish conditions for phantom crossing without phantom scalars.
AI.result: Demonstrated that the scalar field must begin frozen in the radiation era to suppress early coupling and satisfy cosmic microwave background constraints, while allowing strong late-time evolution to match DESI-preferred w_eff(z) behavior, with an example model showing w_eff evolution from about -1.2 at z~1 to -0.9 at z~0.4.
AI.conclusion: Interacting dark energy models with a quintessence field coupled to cold dark matter can effectively mimic phantom crossing in the equation of state without invoking phantom fields, provided the field evolution and coupling behavior satisfy conditions ensuring early universe constraints and late-time dynamics.

title: A GPU-Accelerated JAX Framework for Robust Parametric Component Separation and Clustering Optimization for CMB Polarization Satellites
summary: We present a novel, JAX-powered implementation of a parametric component-separation method for CMB polarization data, explicitly designed to handle spatially varying foreground Spectral Energy Distributions (SEDs). The approach models this variation across the sky by grouping sets of pixels that share common foreground spectral parameters, scanning over thousands of such configurations to evaluate the trade-off between model complexity and residual systematic contamination. Built within the FURAX framework -- a JAX-powered environment for CMB data analysis -- our pipeline extends the fgbuster parametric formalism. It enables fully vectorized, GPU-accelerated evaluation of the spectral likelihood, map reconstruction, and diagnostic metrics across tens of thousands of pixel subset configurations, noise realizations, and sky regions. Our implementation achieves up to $\sim 100\times$ speed-up over the scipy TNC optimizer used in fgbuster when running on GPUs, as well as giving more robust results. When applied to LiteBIRD-like simulations with spatially varying foreground SEDs, our optimized K-means configuration reduces the 68% upper limit on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ by $\approx 30\%$ relative to a fixed, previously derived multi-resolution configuration, while maintaining competitive statistical uncertainties.

AI.tldr: Introduces a GPU-accelerated, JAX-based pipeline for CMB polarization data cleaning that efficiently handles spatially varying foregrounds, achieving a 100× speed increase and 30% better constraints on the tensor-to-scalar ratio compared to previous methods.
AI.motivation: Improve parametric component-separation for CMB polarization data by handling spatially varying foreground SEDs effectively and efficiently.
AI.method: Develop a JAX-powered, GPU-accelerated pipeline within the FURAX framework that models spatial variation by grouping pixels with common spectral parameters, scanning thousands of configurations to balance model complexity and residual contamination, extending the fgbuster formalism with vectorized spectral likelihood evaluation and diagnostics.
AI.result: Achieved up to ~100× speed-up over scipy TNC optimizer on GPUs with more robust results; applying the optimized K-means configuration on LiteBIRD-like simulations reduced the 68% upper limit on the tensor-to-scalar ratio r by ~30% compared to fixed multi-resolution configuration while maintaining competitive uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: The JAX-powered implementation significantly improves both the computational efficiency and accuracy of parametric component separation for CMB polarization data with spatially varying foregrounds, demonstrating substantial gains in constraining cosmological parameters like the tensor-to-scalar ratio.

title: From Internal Collision to Photon Escape: First-Principles Modeling of Radiation-Mediated Shocks in Gamma-Ray Burst Photospheres
summary: Modeling subphotospheric shocks in a gamma-ray burst (GRB) is challenging due to the various timescales that must be resolved, and the fact that the same radiation dynamically mediates the shocks while forming the observed signal. Here, we present the first self-consistent radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a subphotospheric internal collision, following the system from formation and propagation of forward and reverse radiation-mediated shocks all the way to photon decoupling and free streaming toward the observer. The simulation evolves the plasma and photon field with full Compton coupling, including the feedback on the hydrodynamic flow. As the ejecta expands and the optical depth decreases, both shocks broaden and the radiation field becomes highly non-thermal. Surprisingly, we find that the reverse shock remains completely radiation-mediated down to upstream optical depths of order a few $\times 10^{-1}$, which indicates that Compton coupling is important even in moderately optically thin regions. The photons undergo last scattering over a broad range of radii rather than at a single photospheric surface. The light curve shows a late, quasi-thermal post-cursor produced by photons that decouple upstream of the reverse shock, which could be searched for in observations. The emitted time-integrated spectrum is GRB-like, with a low-energy photon index $α\sim -1$ and a high-energy photon index $β\sim -2.5$. These results show how radiation-mediated shocks evolve close to the photosphere and how they shape the emitted photon field.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of subphotospheric shocks in GRBs, revealing that radiation-mediated shocks persist to low optical depths, photons scatter broadly, and the resulting emission matches observed GRB spectral features.
AI.motivation: Modeling subphotospheric shocks in gamma-ray bursts is challenging due to the need to resolve multiple timescales and the interplay between radiation and shock dynamics while forming the observed signal.
AI.method: Performed the first self-consistent radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a subphotospheric internal collision, evolving plasma and photon fields with full Compton coupling, tracking shock formation, propagation, and photon decoupling to free streaming.
AI.result: Found that the reverse shock remains radiation-mediated even at low optical depths (~0.1), that photons last scatter over a range of radii rather than a single surface, and that the time-integrated spectrum resembles observed GRB spectra with specific low and high-energy photon indices. A late quasi-thermal post-cursor in the light curve was predicted.
AI.conclusion: Radiation-mediated shocks near the photosphere evolve in a complex manner shaping the emitted photon field, with significant Compton coupling effects even in moderately optically thin regions, influencing the observed GRB signals.

title: Probing non-Gaussianity during reheating with SIGW in the LISA band
summary: We analyse the effects of a non-standard evolution of the Universe during the reheating epoch on the spectrum of scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) accounting for the presence of primordial non-Gaussianity. We show that given values of $w$ and $c_s^2$ leave characteristic features in the spectrum which can be detectable by third generation interferometers like LISA. In addition, we argue that the specific reheating dynamics can suppress or even enhance the spectrum, with crucial consequences for its detectability. We perform a Fisher forecast for different values of $w$ and different scans to assess the detectability of the signal when different values of the amplitude and central frequency are considered.

AI.tldr: This study investigates how alternative reheating scenarios during the early Universe alter the spectrum of scalar-induced gravitational waves, showing that these effects, influenced by primordial non-Gaussianity, can be detected by future observatories like LISA through characteristic spectral features.
AI.motivation: To understand how non-standard reheating dynamics affect the spectrum of scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs), especially considering primordial non-Gaussianity, and to evaluate the potential detectability of these effects with upcoming interferometers.
AI.method: Analyzing the impact of different values of the equation of state parameter (w) and sound speed squared (c_s^2) on the SIGW spectrum, incorporating primordial non-Gaussianity; performing a Fisher forecast for varying w, amplitude, and central frequency values to assess detectability by third generation interferometers such as LISA.
AI.result: Characteristic features in the SIGW spectrum dependent on w and c_s^2 can be observed, which may be detectable by instruments like LISA. The dynamics of reheating can either suppress or amplify the SIGW spectrum, significantly influencing its observability.
AI.conclusion: Non-standard reheating dynamics imprint distinctive signatures on the SIGW spectrum that affect its amplitude and shape, which can be leveraged by future detectors to probe the reheating epoch and primordial non-Gaussianity.

title: Second-Generation Mass Peak in the Gravitational-Wave Population as a Probe of Globular Clusters
summary: Gravitational-wave observations have revealed an excess of binary black hole mergers with primary masses near $\sim 35\,M_\odot$. We show that if this feature originates from dynamical formation in dense stellar systems, and if the pair-instability supernova truncates the first-generation black hole mass spectrum, then second-generation mergers inevitably produce a second peak near $\sim 70\,M_\odot$. This structure reflects the suppression of first-generation black holes above a characteristic mass and the accumulation of merger remnants near twice that scale. Its location is robust, whereas its amplitude depends strongly on cluster initial conditions. Using a large suite of cluster population-synthesis models, we show that current gravitational-wave data already constrain the birth properties of globular clusters, irrespective of their overall contribution to the observed population. If clusters dominate mergers above the pair-instability scale, these constraints tighten further and imply a minimum first-generation merger rate of $\mathcal{R}(m_1 \leq 50\,M_\odot) \geq 0.099\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ ($99\%$ confidence). We further show that a drop or gap in the secondary black hole mass spectrum is not a robust signature of a cluster origin for high-mass mergers within the pair-instability mass gap. A confirmed excess near $\sim 70\,M_\odot$ would support a dynamical origin of the $\sim 35\,M_\odot$ feature and provide independent evidence for a pair-instability mass gap with a lower edge at $\lesssim 50M_\odot$.

AI.tldr: Gravitational-wave data revealing an excess of black hole mergers near 35 solar masses suggest dynamical formation and pair-instability effects shape the mass spectrum, predicting a second peak near 70 solar masses from second-generation mergers and constraining globular cluster properties and merger rates.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed excess of binary black hole mergers near 35 solar masses and investigate the implications of dynamical formation and pair-instability supernova effects on the black hole mass spectrum.
AI.method: Utilization of a large suite of cluster population-synthesis models to simulate dense stellar system environments and their impact on binary black hole mergers, analyzing the mass distribution features and their dependence on cluster properties.
AI.result: Identification of a predicted second peak in the black hole mass distribution near 70 solar masses caused by second-generation mergers; constraints on the birth properties of globular clusters from gravitational-wave data; demonstration that the presence of a gap in the secondary black hole mass spectrum is not a reliable indicator of cluster origin; and establishment of a minimum first-generation merger rate.
AI.conclusion: The observed 35 solar mass excess likely originates from dynamical formation in dense stellar clusters, with a corresponding robust second peak near 70 solar masses arising from second-generation mergers. This supports the existence of a pair-instability mass gap with a lower edge near 50 solar masses and provides constraints on globular cluster birth properties and merger rates, evidencing a dynamical origin for these black hole mergers.

title: Which Neutron Stars Reach the Stiffening Regime? Multimessenger Constraints on Core Sound Speed and Stellar-Mass Thresholds
summary: We present a concise multimessenger inference of the neutron-star core sound-speed profile using GW170817 and three \textit{NICER} mass--radius posteriors (PSR J0030$+$0451, PSR J0740$+$6620, and PSR J0437$-$4715). The main result is not only a preference for intermediate-density stiffening within smooth equation-of-state families, but a translation of that inference into the stellar masses that access the relevant density regime. In the baseline smooth peaked family, the posterior probability that $c_s^2 > 1/3$ at $3.5\,n_{\rm sat}$ is $85.4\,\%$, while equal-prior averaging over peaked, monotonic, piecewise, and transition-capable families gives a more conservative $79.0\,\%$. Posterior-resampled exact Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff solutions show that the onset density of the inferred stiffening is typically reached near $1.6\,M_\odot$, whereas the peak region is accessed only near $2.1\,M_\odot$. A J0740-like $2.07\,M_\odot$ pulsar reaches the onset in $91\,\%$ of posterior draws but the peak in only $46\,\%$, showing that current data mainly constrain whether massive stars have entered the stiffening regime rather than traversed its full peak.

AI.tldr: Combining gravitational wave and NICER pulsar data reveals that neutron-star cores likely stiffen at intermediate densities, starting around 1.6 solar masses and peaking near 2.1, with current data mainly confirming the onset of this stiffening.
AI.motivation: To infer the sound-speed profile in neutron-star cores using multimessenger astrophysical observations, improving understanding of the equation of state (EoS) at intermediate densities.
AI.method: Combined analysis of gravitational wave data from GW170817 with NICER mass-radius posteriors for three pulsars, using smooth and mixed equation-of-state families along with exact Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff solutions to map sound-speed features to stellar masses.
AI.result: Strong preference for intermediate-density stiffening in the neutron-star equation of state, with high posterior probabilities for the sound speed squared $c_s^2$ exceeding 1/3 at ~3.5 times nuclear saturation density. The inferred stiffening onset typically occurs near 1.6 solar masses and the peak near 2.1 solar masses, with current data more constraining on the onset than the peak of stiffening.
AI.conclusion: Multimessenger data strongly supports a stiffening of the neutron-star core equation of state at intermediate densities, constraining the mass range where this phenomenon occurs, which enhances understanding of dense matter physics in neutron stars.

title: Disentangling cosmic distance tensions with early and late dark energy
summary: Recent cosmological data reveal tension between parameters inferred from measurements of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), and supernovae (SN) under $Λ$CDM. Typical dynamical dark energy parameterizations (such as $w_0w_a$) that seek to jointly resolve these tensions have an equation of state parameter that crosses into the phantom regime, leading to potential instabilities for physical models. We show that the BAO (early-time) and SN (late-time) sides of the tension can instead be treated independently. Early dark energy (EDE) can reduce the tension between CMB-BAO data by changing the calibration of the sound horizon at the drag epoch $r_d$, with a $Δχ^2 = -{9.4}$ relative to $Λ$CDM, raising $H_0$ to 70.87 $\rm km s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}$. EDE alone cannot bring consistency between CMB, BAO, and SN data, but combining with a thawing-quintessence component of dark energy reduces tensions between the three datasets, with $Δχ^2=-12.6$ relative to $Λ$CDM without a phantom component, vs. $Δχ^2=-15.8$ for $w_0 w_a$ with one. We consider different SN datasets, using the most recent DES Dovekie catalog as our default while assessing differences with the original DESY5 and Pantheon+ catalogs. While the significance of adding thawing quintessence changes, the EDE solution to the CMB-BAO tension remains nearly unaffected. Moreover, though we do not include direct Hubble constant measurements in these $Δχ^2$ values, the EDE solution reduces the Hubble tension with the Local Distance Network value from $7σ$ in $Λ$CDM to $2-3σ$ depending on the SN dataset, nominally the equivalent of an extra $Δχ^2 \sim -40$ or more.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes resolving cosmological parameter tensions between CMB, BAO, and SN data by introducing early dark energy and thawing quintessence, avoiding phantom dark energy instabilities. This approach significantly reduces the Hubble tension and improves model fits compared to ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To address the tension between cosmological parameters inferred from CMB, BAO, and SN data under the standard ΛCDM model, especially without invoking phantom dark energy models that lead to instabilities.
AI.method: Separately treating BAO (early-time) and SN (late-time) tensions by introducing early dark energy (EDE) to modify the sound horizon calibration and combining EDE with a thawing-quintessence dark energy component. Different SN datasets, including DES Dovekie, DESY5, and Pantheon+, were analyzed to assess robustness.
AI.result: EDE reduces the CMB-BAO tension significantly, raising H0 to ~70.87 km/s/Mpc, but cannot alone reconcile all data. Combining EDE with thawing quintessence further reduces tensions among CMB, BAO, and SN datasets without requiring phantom crossing, achieving Δχ2=-12.6 compared to ΛCDM, close to the more negative Δχ2 for phantom w0wa models. EDE also lowers the Hubble tension with Local Distance Network measurements from 7σ to 2-3σ, akin to an improvement of Δχ2 ~ -40 or more.
AI.conclusion: Separating early- and late-time cosmological tensions and utilizing an early dark energy model combined with a thawing-quintessence component provides a stable and effective resolution of parameter tensions without phantom instabilities, significantly alleviating the Hubble tension and improving fit quality relative to ΛCDM.

title: Detection of TeV emission during early afterglow from poorly localized GRBs with ground based IACTs
summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most luminous and rapidly evolving transients in the Universe. While space-based instruments have extended GRB observations up to energies of $\sim$100 GeV, the detection of very-high-energy (VHE; $E>100$ GeV) emission from ground-based telescopes, especially during prompt or/and the early afterglow phase, remains challenging. These difficulties arise from the rapid temporal decay of GRB afterglows, strong attenuation by the extragalactic background light (EBL), observational latency, and the typical poor sky localization provided by MeV-detectors such as Fermi/GBM. In this work, we investigate the prospects for detecting TeV ($\sim$100 GeV--1 TeV) emission from poorly localized GRBs by adopting optimized follow-up strategies based on rapid tiling of large localization regions. We simulate a realistic population of GRBs informed by more than fifteen years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT detections and recent progresses in the afterglow emission modeling. Using these simulations, we evaluate the detectability of GRB early afterglows by the next-generation Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes, equipped with larger field-of-view (FoV), as a function of latency, exposure time, and observational strategy. Our strategy can significantly enhance the detection rate; for instruments such as ASTRI and LACT, it increases by up to a factor of two compared to strategies limited to well-localized (Swift-like) events. For CTAO, our proposed approach provides up to four VHE detections per year.

AI.tldr: This study uses simulations to show that optimized rapid-tiling follow-up strategies with next-generation Cherenkov telescopes can double or quadruple detection rates of very-high-energy gamma-ray bursts, overcoming challenges of poor localization and fast afterglow decay.
AI.motivation: Detecting very-high-energy (VHE) emission from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), especially during their prompt or early afterglow phases, is challenging due to rapid afterglow decay, extragalactic background light attenuation, observational delays, and poor sky localization from MeV detectors.
AI.method: Simulated a realistic population of GRBs based on over fifteen years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT data and afterglow emission models; evaluated detectability of early afterglows by next-generation Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes using optimized rapid-tiling follow-up strategies over large localization regions, considering factors such as latency, exposure time, and observational strategy.
AI.result: Optimized follow-up with rapid tiling significantly improves detection rates of TeV emission from poorly localized GRBs; detection rates can increase by up to a factor of two for instruments like ASTRI and LACT, and up to four VHE detections per year for CTAO.
AI.conclusion: Implementing optimized rapid-tiling observational strategies enhances the prospects of detecting TeV emission from GRBs with next-gen Cherenkov telescopes, even for poorly localized bursts, improving detection rates substantially compared to conventional strategies focused on well-localized events.

title: Isolating Sgr A East: The First Uncontaminated X-ray Maps of a Galactic Center Supernova Remnant
comment: 25 pages, 4 tables, 14 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The central few parsecs of the Milky Way host a complex X-ray-emitting environment in which several extended plasma components are blended along the line of sight, complicating attempts to measure the intrinsic properties of individual components. In particular, the supernova remnant (SNR) Sgr A East is strongly confused with the stellar wind-fed plasma associated with Sagittarius A* and the surrounding nuclear environment. Here we apply Poissonian Generalized Morphological Component Analysis (pGMCA) to deep, stacked Chandra ACIS-I observations of the Galactic Center to disentangle these overlapping X-ray components. By comparing the separated X-ray components with multiwavelength data, we identify the location of the reflected shock in Sgr A East and construct spatially resolved maps of Fe and S/Ar/Ca emission. The Fe emission is centrally concentrated, consistent with the properties of mixed-morphology supernova remnants. Separating the SNR emission from the shocked wind plasma around Sgr A* allows us to recover uncontaminated SNR properties and improve the robustness of the derived parameters. Spectral modeling of the isolated Sgr A East component reveals a lower ionization age and a higher electron density than previously reported, indicating strong interaction with dense surrounding material.

AI.tldr: They used advanced morphological analysis on deep X-ray data to separate overlapping plasma emissions in the Galactic Center, isolating the Sgr A East supernova remnant and revealing its interaction with dense material, improving understanding of its intrinsic properties.
AI.motivation: The complex X-ray environment in the Galactic Center blends multiple plasma components, complicating individual source characterization, particularly for the Sgr A East supernova remnant (SNR) which is confused with plasma around Sagittarius A*.
AI.method: Applied Poissonian Generalized Morphological Component Analysis (pGMCA) to deep, stacked Chandra ACIS-I observations to disentangle overlapping X-ray emission components, complemented by multiwavelength data comparison.
AI.result: Identified the reflected shock location in Sgr A East and constructed spatially resolved maps of Fe and S/Ar/Ca emission. The Fe emission is centrally concentrated, consistent with mixed-morphology SNRs. Separation of SNR from shocked wind plasma yielded uncontaminated SNR parameters showing lower ionization age and higher electron density than prior reports, indicating strong interaction with dense material.
AI.conclusion: Using pGMCA effectively disentangles confused X-ray components in the Galactic Center, enabling precise characterization of Sgr A East. The refined spectral analysis reveals that Sgr A East is strongly interacting with dense surrounding plasma, revising previous estimates of its physical conditions.

title: Development of Faster and More Accurate Supernova Localization at Super-Kamiokande
summary: The next nearby core-collapse supernova (SN) promises to yield a treasure of scientific information through multi-messenger astronomy. Early observations of the shock breakout (SBO) emissions are especially critical to understand the SN explosive mechanism as well as the properties of the progenitor star. Neutrino observatories are able to provide an early alert of a SN before the arrival of the SBO radiation. Super-Kamiokande (SK) has the unique capability to independently reconstruct an accurate SN pointing direction as part of its real-time monitoring system, ``SNWATCH.'' Recent upgrades to SK by adding gadolinium (Gd) to the detection volume have been accompanied by efforts to improve the speed and accuracy of SN direction reconstruction. A new, novel HEALPix-based approach (``HP-Fitter'') can calculate the SN direction from the reconstructed burst event directions in less than one second. As well, the previous maximum-likelihood direction fitter (``ML-Fitter'') was upgraded by incorporating event information from Gd neutron-capture as well as using the HP-Fitter for the initial fit parameters and from code refactoring and optimization. The improved ML-Fitter has better angular resolution but direction reconstruction time is $\mathcal{O}$(sec). Together with improvements in burst detection and event reconstruction times, SNWATCH is now able to generate an SN alert with pointing information in about 90 seconds. These upgrades have been implemented at SK and integrated into a new automated system to provide GCN notices.

AI.tldr: Upgrades to Super-Kamiokande's real-time supernova monitoring system, including novel direction reconstruction algorithms and gadolinium-enhanced detection, enable fast (∼90 s) and accurate SN pointing alerts to advance multi-messenger astronomy.
AI.motivation: Provide early alerts of core-collapse supernovae with accurate pointing information to facilitate multi-messenger astronomy and improve understanding of supernova mechanisms and progenitor properties.
AI.method: Implemented a novel HEALPix-based direction reconstruction method (HP-Fitter) for rapid SN direction estimation and upgraded the existing maximum-likelihood fitter (ML-Fitter) to incorporate gadolinium neutron-capture event data, using HP-Fitter outputs for initial parameters and optimizing code for improved speed and accuracy.
AI.result: The combined upgrades enable the Super-Kamiokande SNWATCH system to generate supernova alerts with pointing information within approximately 90 seconds, offering better angular resolution and faster response times.
AI.conclusion: The integration of the HP-Fitter and upgraded ML-Fitter with gadolinium-enhanced detection volume significantly improves the speed and accuracy of supernova direction reconstruction in SK, enabling timely and precise SN alerts for multi-messenger observations.

title: Resolving the 2024 Outburst of Magnetar 1E 1841-045 from its host Supernova Remnant with EP-FXT
summary: The magnetar 1E 1841-045 exhibited a new active episode starting on August 20, 2024, marked by X-ray bursts and enhanced persistent emission. Using data from the Einstein Probe (EP), we report on the timing and spectral results following the onset of this outburst. The pulse profile displays a multi-peaked structure, with notable phase shifts in the secondary peak. Energy-resolved pulse profile analysis indicates a transition in the dominant peak of the pulse profile above 5.8 keV. The 0.5-10 keV X-ray spectrum is well-modeled by a combined blackbody and power-law (BB+PL) model, showing a $\sim 20\%$ flux increase following the outburst. Phase-resolved spectroscopy indicates a correlation between BB temperature and pulse profile intensity, along with spectral hardening at a specific pulse phase. The high spatial resolution of EP enables effective separation of the supernova remnant emission, which is crucial for measuring the intrinsic pulse emission of the source. These findings underscore the intricate relationship between magnetar outbursts, pulse profile evolution, and spectral characteristics.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the 2024 outburst of magnetar 1E 1841-045 using Einstein Probe data, revealing changes in pulse profile and spectrum linked to the outburst, with spectral and timing features indicating complex emission dynamics.
AI.motivation: To investigate the timing and spectral evolution of the magnetar 1E 1841-045 during its new active episode and understand the relationship between the outburst and changes in pulse profile and spectral properties.
AI.method: Using observations from the Einstein Probe, the study analyzes the timing and energy-resolved pulse profiles, and performs phase-resolved spectroscopy to model the X-ray emission before and after the outburst, separating intrinsic emission from the supernova remnant background.
AI.result: The magnetar exhibited a multi-peaked pulse profile with phase shifts and a dominant peak transition above 5.8 keV. The X-ray spectrum fits a combined blackbody plus power-law model with about 20% flux increase post-outburst, showing correlations between blackbody temperature and pulse intensity and spectral hardening at specific phases. Separating supernova remnant emission was critical to isolate the magnetar's intrinsic emission.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate a complex interplay between magnetar outbursts, evolving pulse profile structures, and spectral changes, highlighting the importance of phase-resolved spectral analysis in understanding magnetar emission mechanisms.

authors: Z. G. Wen S. N. Sun
title: A study of periodic nulling in PSR B0751+32 with FAST
comment: 8 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We report new results from a nulling study of PSR~B0751+32 (PSR J0754+3231), observed at 1250~MHz with the Five hundred meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). Our analysis confirms the presence of periodic nulling in this pulsar. Using the recently developed mixture model method, we obtained a nulling fraction (NF) of $35.1\% \pm 0.6\%$. Three independent approaches were employed to estimate the nulling periodicity, and the results reveal significant temporal evolution of the modulation both within individual observations and across different \textbf{observing} essions. The pulsar exhibits an asymmetric two-component mean pulse profile, with the leading component brighter and narrower than the trailing one. Pulse energy analysis shows that both components remain stable immediately after the onset of the burst state, but subsequently undergo a progressive decline, with the trailing component most severely affected prior to burst termination. Notably, no evidence of the previously reported subpulse drifting was detected in our data. Our results challenge previous models that ascribed periodic nulling to purely geometric effects.

AI.tldr: Using FAST observations, this study confirms periodic nulling in PSR B0751+32 with a 35% nulling fraction and reveals evolving nulling patterns and pulse energy changes, challenging prior geometric explanations.
AI.motivation: To investigate and better understand the nulling behavior and periodicity of pulsar PSR B0751+32 using high sensitivity observations from FAST.
AI.method: Observing PSR B0751+32 at 1250 MHz with FAST; applying a mixture model method to estimate nulling fraction; employing three independent approaches to estimate nulling periodicity; performing pulse energy analysis on the two pulse profile components.
AI.result: Confirmed presence of periodic nulling with a nulling fraction of 35.1% ± 0.6%. Identified temporal evolution of nulling modulation within and across observing sessions. The pulsar has a two-component asymmetric pulse profile with differential energy decline prior to burst termination. No subpulse drifting detected. Findings challenge previous geometric models of nulling.
AI.conclusion: Periodic nulling in PSR B0751+32 is dynamic and not solely due to geometric effects, implying more complex underlying mechanisms influencing nulling behavior.

title: Does the spectral break in the IceCube diffuse neutrino spectrum originate from AGN evolution?
summary: The enigmatic origin of the diffuse neutrino background detected by IceCube in the energy range from TeV to PeV remains one of the central open problems in high-energy astrophysics, and this puzzle is further deepened by the recent evidence for a spectral break. Could this convex-spectrum background arise predominantly from the evolution of active galactic nuclei (AGNs)? In this work, we claim that the spectral break is naturally predicted when AGN evolution is taken into account, and the diffuse flux can be interpreted as the superposition of contributions from AGNs at different evolutionary phases. We develop a unified framework that incorporates AGN evolution, where cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated during the active phase subsequently diffuse and interact in the host galaxy after the central engine switches off, producing a long-lived hadronic afterglow. Adopting physically plausible parameters, our model successfully reproduces both the spectral features of the diffuse background and the observed neutrino emission from representative sources such as TXS 0506$+$056 and NGC 1068. Our results suggest that AGN host galaxies are more efficient CR reservoirs than previously expected. Moreover, the model favors a lepton-dominated scenario for most AGNs. This conclusion accounts for the relatively low detection rate of point-like sources by IceCube and underscores the need for next-generation neutrino telescopes with larger effective areas and higher sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified AGN evolution model that explains the diffuse neutrino background’s spectral break as a result of cosmic rays producing hadronic afterglows in AGN host galaxies, matching observational data and suggesting AGNs are key contributors to high-energy neutrinos.
AI.motivation: To investigate the origin of the diffuse neutrino background detected by IceCube, particularly addressing the spectral break observed and the role of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in producing this background.
AI.method: Developing a unified framework incorporating AGN evolution where cosmic rays accelerated during AGN active phases diffuse and interact within the host galaxy post central engine shutdown, generating a hadronic afterglow. The model uses physically plausible parameters and compares predictions with observed neutrino emissions from sources like TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068.
AI.result: The model naturally predicts the spectral break and reproduces the spectral features of the diffuse neutrino background as well as neutrino emissions from specific AGNs. It highlights that AGN host galaxies are efficient cosmic ray reservoirs and supports a lepton-dominated scenario for most AGNs, explaining the low detection rate of point-like neutrino sources by IceCube.
AI.conclusion: The diffuse neutrino background with a spectral break can be explained by the evolutionary phases of AGNs, where cosmic ray interactions in host galaxies produce a hadronic afterglow. This supports the idea that AGNs significantly contribute to the diffuse neutrino flux and motivates the development of more sensitive and larger neutrino observatories.

title: The deci-Hz gravitational wave signal from the collapse of rotating very massive stars
summary: We calculate the gravitational wave signal from the collapse of a rotating 300 $M_\odot$ star at the upper end of the pair-instability regime. The large-scale asymmetries that develop during the collapse produce a strong signal in the deci-Hz range that has a characteristic shape which is likely amenable to a template-based search. The most ambitious designs for deci-Hz detectors could detect such signals out to distances of 200 Mpc, possibly at a rate of 0.5 per year.

AI.tldr: The study predicts that rotating 300 solar mass stars collapsing via pair-instability produce strong, distinctive gravitational waves in the deci-Hz range, potentially detectable by future observatories up to 200 Mpc away with a moderate event rate.
AI.motivation: To explore gravitational wave signals from massive stellar collapse within the pair-instability regime, particularly focusing on signals from rotating 300 solar mass stars.
AI.method: Performed calculations of gravitational wave emission during the collapse of a rotating 300 solar mass star, analyzing asymmetries and signal characteristics in the deci-Hz frequency range.
AI.result: Identified strong gravitational wave signals with distinctive waveform shapes suitable for template-based searches, detectable up to 200 Mpc by future deci-Hz detectors, with an expected detection rate of about 0.5 events per year.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational waves from the collapse of massive rotating stars at the pair-instability threshold represent promising targets for next-generation deci-Hz gravitational wave observatories, offering detectable signals over cosmologically significant distances at an appreciable event rate.

title: Oblique Shocks at Supernova Remnants in Massive Star Clusters: A Model for the Cosmic-Ray Knee Observed by LHAASO
comment: 23 pages,8 figures, accepted in Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
summary: This work establishes oblique shocks in Massive Star Clusters (MSC) as a primary mechanism for accelerating cosmic rays (CR) up to the knee of the energy spectrum. We develop a model that incorporates the combined contribution of supernova and collective wind shocks, emphasizing the critical role of the shock obliquity angle in determining the maximum particle energy. We illustrate, within our model that oblique shocks can significantly enhance acceleration efficiency, allowing particles to reach multi-PeV energies in a rigidity-dependent manner. Our preferred model, which incorporates oblique shocks, reproduces the all-particle spectrum and composition observed by The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO), interpreting the knee as arising from a sequence of rigidity-dependent cutoffs. The model also predicts subdominant but detectable gamma-ray and neutrino emissions. This study provides an attempt at building a unified framework connecting MSC particle acceleration to the observed features of the cosmic-ray knee.

AI.tldr: This paper models oblique shocks in Massive Star Clusters as the main driver for accelerating cosmic rays up to the knee energy, successfully reproducing observed spectra and predicting related gamma-ray and neutrino signals.
AI.motivation: To identify the primary mechanism behind cosmic ray acceleration up to the knee energy in Massive Star Clusters (MSC).
AI.method: Development of a model integrating supernova and collective wind shocks with emphasis on shock obliquity angle's influence on maximum particle energy.
AI.result: Oblique shocks substantially enhance acceleration efficiency, enabling particles to reach multi-PeV energies with rigidity-dependent cutoffs that align with observational data from LHAASO.
AI.conclusion: Oblique shocks in MSC serve as a key acceleration mechanism explaining the cosmic ray knee's features, linking particle acceleration processes with observed cosmic ray spectra and associated gamma-ray and neutrino emissions.

title: Flux variability of the "10 keV feature" of 4U 0115+63
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 15 pages, 11 figures
summary: X-ray spectra of accretion-powered X-ray pulsars can often be described using a power-law continuum with a high-energy cutoff, which might be further modified by additional spectral components. The Be X-ray binary system 4U 0115+63 is well known for having one of the highest numbers of detected harmonics of its cyclotron resonant scattering features (CRSFs), a pronounced spectral component known as the ''10 keV feature,'' and quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) with a period of about 500 s during outbursts. The changes in count rate by a factor of two during the approximately 500 s QPOs allow us to probe the variation in the spectral components with flux. We study the ''10 keV feature'' in emission, aiming to disentangle it from the broadband continuum and CRSFs and investigate its origin. We focus on the flux-dependent behavior of the CRSF and its harmonics, and particularly the contribution of the ''10 keV feature,'' as seen in the flux-resolved analysis of two NuSTAR observations of the 2015 outburst. Comparing the flux-resolved spectra of a given observation with the respective total dataset revealed a distinct change in overall spectral shape at the position of the ''10 keV feature'' but no comparable deviation at the energies of the harmonic CRSFs. The change associated with the ''10 keV feature'' does not seem to involve its centroid energy, which remains constant within a given observation. We find indications for an anticorrelation between the continuum flux and the ratio of the ''10 keV feature'' flux to the continuum flux within each observation. The analysis strengthens previous claims that the ''10 keV feature'' shows some independence from the remaining features. This result supports the interpretation that the ''10 keV feature'' has a different formation mechanism than the continuum emission, although its origin lies within the same physical environment.

AI.tldr: Analysis of flux-resolved NuSTAR data from 4U 0115+63 shows the ''10 keV feature'' behaves distinctly from cyclotron lines, with constant centroid energy and flux-dependent strength, suggesting a unique formation mechanism separate from the continuum and CRSFs.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature and origin of the ''10 keV feature'' in the X-ray spectra of the Be X-ray binary system 4U 0115+63 and understand its relation to the cyclotron resonant scattering features (CRSFs) and continuum emission, especially under flux variability observed in quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs).
AI.method: Performed flux-resolved spectral analysis of two NuSTAR observations from the 2015 outburst of 4U 0115+63, comparing flux-dependent changes in spectral components including the ''10 keV feature'' and multiple harmonic CRSFs to disentangle their respective behaviors.
AI.result: The ''10 keV feature'' exhibits a distinct flux-dependent change in overall spectral shape with a constant centroid energy, differing from the harmonic CRSFs which show no comparable spectral deviation. An anticorrelation was found between the continuum flux and the flux ratio of the ''10 keV feature'' to the continuum within each observation, indicating its partial independence from other spectral features.
AI.conclusion: The study supports that the ''10 keV feature'' originates from a different formation mechanism than the continuum emission and CRSFs, although it exists in the same physical environment. This confirms the feature’s unique spectral behavior and flux dependence within the accretion-powered X-ray pulsar system.

title: How many VHE gamma-ray binaries with young pulsars can be observed?
comment: 25 pages, 10 figures, published in Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
summary: A population of Galactic gamma-ray binaries is currently emerging due to ever increasing sensitivity of gamma-ray observatories. The detection of very high energy (VHE) photons with energies well above 10 TeV from a dozen of sources and the estimated power of those sources make them potentially interesting cosmic ray accelerators. Multi-wavelength observations of gamma-ray binaries revealed that most of them include a young massive star in pair with a relativistic companion, either a black hole or energetic pulsar. Fast stellar winds interacting with powerful relativistic outflows from pulsars or the black hole jets in microquasars are favorable sites for VHE particle acceleration. To estimate the expected number of gamma-ray binaries, we present results of population synthesis calculations of Galactic binaries in which a young massive OB- or Be-star is accompanied by a pulsar capable of producing a powerful relativistic outflow. The distributions over the binary eccentricities, orbital periods, Be-disk inclinations, and the pulsar braking energy losses are taken into account. Conditions for a binary to accelerate VHE particles, radiate and absorb the non-thermal photons that may reach the observer are discussed. We model the anisotropic structure of the zone of interaction of the relativistic pulsar wind with the strongly magnetized massive star's wind. The stellar winds with strong ($\sim$ Gauss) magnetic fields at $\sim$ AU distances colliding with powerful pulsar outflows are capable of accelerating particles up to PeV energies at some orbital configurations and phases. The strong magnetic field in the interaction region produces a highly anisotropic structure of the particle accelerator and emitter in the pulsar outflow. The anisotropic radiation pattern may affect the gamma-ray photon absorption and the number of the observed gamma-ray loud systems.

AI.tldr: This study models Galactic gamma-ray binaries formed by massive stars and pulsars, showing their wind interactions can accelerate particles to PeV energies and produce anisotropic gamma-ray emission, which influences the observed population of these sources.
AI.motivation: To understand the emerging population of Galactic gamma-ray binaries as potential cosmic ray accelerators due to increasing sensitivity of gamma-ray observatories.
AI.method: Population synthesis calculations of binaries with a young massive OB- or Be-star and a pulsar, accounting for distributions in eccentricities, orbital periods, Be-disk inclinations, and pulsar energy losses. Modeling of anisotropic interaction zones between pulsar and stellar winds was performed.
AI.result: Identified that colliding winds with strong magnetic fields at AU scale can accelerate particles to PeV energies in specific orbital configurations. Anisotropic radiation and magnetic fields influence photon absorption and observed gamma-ray emission patterns.
AI.conclusion: Gamma-ray binaries with young massive stars and pulsar companions can serve as PeV particle accelerators. Their anisotropic wind interactions and magnetic fields shape the emission and absorption of very high energy photons, affecting the visibility of these sources in gamma rays.

title: The Stack Search Tests on FAST Data: Discovery of Six Faint Isolated Millisecond Pulsars in NGC 6517 and NGC 7078 (M15)
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL; 10 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables
summary: We report the discovery of six faint millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the globular clusters NGC 6517 and NGC 7078 (M15) using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). These discoveries were enabled by stacking power spectra from multiple observations, a method that effectively boosts the signal-to-noise ratio of faint sources. In NGC 6517, we identified four new MSPs (NGC 6517S-V) with spin periods ranging from 3.68 to 6.02 ms and dispersion measures (DMs) between 182.45 and 182.85 pc cm^-3. In M15, two additional MSPs (M15M and M15N) were discovered, with spin periods of 4.83 and 9.28 ms, and DMs of 67.89 and 66.65 pc cm^-3, respectively. A phase-coherent timing solution has been obtained for M15M; however, sparse detection rates currently preclude phase-connected solutions for the remaining five pulsars. Current timing parameters suggest all six MSPs are isolated, which is consistent with the expected pulsar populations in core-collapsed globular clusters. Notably, pulsars M15N, NGC 6517U, and NGC 6517V eluded detection by standard frequency-domain searches (e.g., PRESTO-based) and the Fast Folding Algorithm, demonstrating that the stack search technique significantly enhances detection sensitivity to inherently faint pulsar signals.

AI.tldr: By stacking power spectra from multiple observations, six faint MSPs were discovered in two globular clusters using FAST, demonstrating improved detection sensitivity over traditional methods.
AI.motivation: To detect faint millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in globular clusters that are challenging to identify using conventional search methods.
AI.method: Stacking power spectra from multiple observations to improve signal-to-noise ratio, enabling detection of faint pulsars.
AI.result: Discovery of six new MSPs in globular clusters NGC 6517 and NGC 7078 (M15), including four in NGC 6517 and two in M15, with detailed timing solutions obtained for at least one pulsar.
AI.conclusion: Stack search technique effectively enhances sensitivity for detecting faint MSPs that standard methods miss, expanding our understanding of pulsar populations in core-collapsed globular clusters.

title: Stochastic problems in pulsar timing
summary: Langevin stochastic differential equations provide a dynamical description of pulsar timing noise and gravitational wave background (GWB) signals. They are also central to state space algorithms that have gained traction in pulsar timing array analysis due to their linear computational scaling with the number of observations. In this work, we utilize established methods in diffusion theory to derive analytical solutions (means, covariances, and probability density functions) to Langevin equations relevant to red noise and the GWB signal in pulsars. The solutions give direct physical insight on the dynamics of pulsar timing signals. As a canonical example, we show that the pulsar spin frequency modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is mathematically inconsistent with a stationary GWB signal when the timing residual is the direct observable. The nonstationarity can be partially dealt with by marginalizing over long time deterministic trends in the data. Then, we show that a random process based on an overdamped harmonic oscillator supports both a stationary spin frequency and phase residuals, consistent with a stationary GWB signal. We also turn our attention to a phenomenological model of a neutron star -- a two-component model with spin wandering -- that has been motivated to explain observed timing noise in radio pulsars. We derive analytical expressions for the means, covariances, and cross-covariances of the crust and superfluid rotational states driven by white noise. The associated constant deterministic torques are linked to the quadratic spin-down of pulsars. The solutions reveal the physical origin of nonstationarity in the residual model: the coexistence of damped and diffusive eigenmodes of the system.

AI.tldr: This paper derives analytical solutions to Langevin equations for pulsar timing noise and gravitational wave background signals, reveals limitations of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model, proposes a stationary overdamped harmonic oscillator model, and explains timing noise nonstationarity with a two-component neutron star model.
AI.motivation: To provide a dynamical and analytical description of pulsar timing noise and gravitational wave background signals using Langevin stochastic differential equations, improving the physical understanding and computational methods in pulsar timing array analysis.
AI.method: Utilized established diffusion theory methods to derive analytical solutions (means, covariances, probability density functions) to Langevin equations modeling red noise and GWB signals; analyzed the mathematical consistency of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and overdamped harmonic oscillator models for pulsar spin and timing residuals; derived analytical expressions for a two-component neutron star spin wandering model driven by white noise.
AI.result: Found that the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process for pulsar spin frequency is inconsistent with a stationary GWB signal when timing residuals are observables; demonstrated that an overdamped harmonic oscillator model supports stationary spin frequency and phase residuals compatible with GWB; revealed that the two-component neutron star model explains timing noise nonstationarity via damped and diffusive eigenmodes, linking deterministic torques to quadratic spin-down.
AI.conclusion: Analytical solutions of Langevin equations provide direct physical insight into pulsar timing noise dynamics and gravitational wave backgrounds; proper modeling requires accounting for stationarity conditions and physical processes such as overdamped harmonic oscillations and spin wandering; these findings enhance the understanding of nonstationarity origins and improve pulsar timing array data analysis.

title: A parametric study of plasma instability cooling and its impact on intergalactic magnetic field constraints in GeV cascades
summary: Electromagnetic cascades are initiated by TeV gamma rays propagating through the intergalactic medium (IGM), and they can be used to constrain the weak intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF) in cosmic voids. Primary TeV photons produce electrons and positrons through electromagnetic pair production, which can be deflected out of the line-of-sight to the observer by IGMF. In addition, electron-positron pairs can perturb the IGM, triggering plasma instabilities that can cool down the pairs before they upscatter cosmic background photons to GeV energies via inverse Compton (IC) scattering. We investigate the influence of plasma instabilities on the cascade spectrum by introducing a parameterized model for the instability using a publicly available Monte Carlo framework CRPropa. We use extended-emission observations within the field of view of the observer to constrain the IGMF in the presence of plasma instability cooling. Based on spectral observations of the blazar 1ES 0229+200 from Fermi-LAT, we find the best-fit photon spectrum including the plasma instability and IGMF parameters that reproduces the observational data for different observer field-of-view angles and obtain the IGMF constraint in cosmic voids. We find that plasma instabilities with a characteristic length scale of order $10^{2}~\text{kpc}$ reproduce the observed photon spectrum and imply an IGMF strength of order $10^{-17}~\text{G}$.

AI.tldr: The paper models plasma instabilities in electromagnetic cascades initiated by TeV gamma rays and uses Fermi-LAT blazar observations to constrain the intergalactic magnetic field, finding a field strength around 10^{-17} G in cosmic voids influenced by plasma instability cooling.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of plasma instabilities on the electromagnetic cascade spectrum initiated by TeV gamma rays propagating through the intergalactic medium, and to use this understanding to better constrain the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF) in cosmic voids.
AI.method: The study introduces a parameterized model for plasma instabilities within the electromagnetic cascade framework using the Monte Carlo simulation tool CRPropa. It involves analyzing extended gamma-ray emissions in the observer's field of view and fitting the cascade photon spectrum to spectral observations from the blazar 1ES 0229+200 obtained by Fermi-LAT, considering different observer field-of-view angles.
AI.result: The best-fit photon spectrum that includes plasma instability effects and IGMF parameters reproduces the observational data well. Plasma instabilities with a characteristic length scale around 100 kpc explain the observed spectrum and suggest an IGMF strength on the order of 10^{-17} G in cosmic voids.
AI.conclusion: Plasma instabilities notably affect the electromagnetic cascade spectrum by cooling electron-positron pairs and must be included in models to accurately constrain the IGMF. The findings indicate an intergalactic magnetic field strength of approximately 10^{-17} G in cosmic voids, inferred from spectral observations considering these plasma effects.

title: Optical images of Kerr-Sen black hole illuminated by thick accretion disks
summary: This paper investigates the shadow and polarization images of a Kerr-Sen black hole illuminated by geometrically thick and optically thin accretion disks. We adopt two classes of accretion models, namely the phenomenological radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) model and the analytical ballistic approximation accretion flow (BAAF) model. Based on radiative transfer theory, we examine the effects of the spin parameter $a$, black hole charge $Q$, and observer inclination angle $θ$ on the shadow images. Both models show that, as the charge $Q$ increases, the photon rings and the central dark regions shrink simultaneously. Meanwhile, frame dragging gives rise to a pronounced brightness asymmetry, which becomes more significant with increasing $a$ and $θ$. The main difference between isotropic and anisotropic radiation is that, in the latter case, the higher order images are brighter in the upper and lower polar regions. For the BAAF model, because the conical approximation renders certain regions geometrically thinner, the spatial extent of the higher order images is narrower than that in the RIAF model, and the separation between the direct image and the higher order images is more distinct. In the polarization images, the spatial distribution of the polarization vector directions is mainly determined by gravitational lensing and frame dragging, whereas the intensity near the photon ring and the scale of the higher order images are significantly influenced by $Q$.

AI.tldr: This paper models shadow and polarization images of Kerr-Sen black holes using two accretion flow models, showing how black hole charge, spin, and viewing angle affect image features and brightness asymmetries, with key differences between isotropic and anisotropic radiation and between RIAF and BAAF models.
AI.motivation: To understand how the spin, charge, and observer inclination affect the shadow and polarization images of Kerr-Sen black holes surrounded by thick, optically thin accretion disks.
AI.method: Two accretion flow models, the radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) and the ballistic approximation accretion flow (BAAF), are applied along with radiative transfer theory to simulate shadow and polarization images.
AI.result: Increasing black hole charge $Q$ shrinks photon rings and central dark regions; frame dragging causes brightness asymmetry enhanced by spin $a$ and inclination $θ$; anisotropic radiation brightens higher order images in polar regions; BAAF model shows narrower higher order image extents and clearer image separations compared to RIAF; polarization vector distribution is dominated by gravitational lensing and frame dragging, with intensity near photon ring influenced by $Q$.
AI.conclusion: The study delineates how Kerr-Sen black hole parameters and accretion flow models distinctly influence shadow and polarization image features, highlighting the roles of black hole charge, spin, observer angle, and radiation anisotropy in shaping observational signatures.
